full_judgment:
10. Mr. Subrata Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 1, has raised the preliminary objection that in writ jurisdiction there is no power of this Court to review a decision once given. He contends that as orders were passed on 7.5.91, this Court is functus officio and cannot change them on any ground whatsoever. He further submits that as the petitioner did not appear to contest the Rule and controvert the facts stated in the writ petition, he cannot now come with the application for review of the orders passed by this Court. He has also submitted that the petition is barred by limitation. 

 17. On the question of limitation, we find that it has been stated by the petitioner that he came to know of the judgment dated 7.5.91 in Writ Petition No. 2551 of 1990 when he came to Dhaka on 6.6.91 and obtained a certified copy on the same day. It was then that he found that respondent No. 1 by suppressing material facts and practising fraud upon this Court he got the Rule made absolute. Accordingly he filed this review petition and swore affidavit on 9.6.91 that is 3 days after he found that fraud had been committed on the Court. 

 18. If fraud is proved, then there is no question, of limitation and it will run from the date when fraud was detected. This view was held by the Appellate Division in the case of Abul Khair Mia Vs. Abdul Latif Sardar reported in 32 DLR (AD) 167. Relianee may be placed on the cases of Abdul Rou] Vs. Abdul Hamid Khan 17 DLR (SC) 515=1965 PLD (SC) 671 and Sailur Rahman Vs. Haider Shah, 19 DLR (SC) 433, In the instant case the petitioner had discovered on 6.6.91 that fraud had been committed on this Court and filed his review petition on 9.6.91 that is, three days after the discovery of fraud. Therefore there has been no delay in filing the review petition and is not barred by limitation. Turning to the question of suppression of facts by respondent No. 1 it appears from Annexure 'F' to the Writ Petition No. 2551 of 1990 that the affidavit to the writ petition was sworn on behalf of respondent No. 1 that is the petitioner of the writ petition on 22.11.90 and a Rule Nisi was issued on 26.11.90. It is admitted that the respondent No. 1 as plaintiff had filed the Title Suit No. 12 of 1990 before the Assistant Judge, Balagunj challenging the order under Memo. No. Matsya/ Bala/125/1(2) dated 18.6.90 passed by the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Balaganj cancelling the lease of the respondent No. 1 and the order of lease granted in favour of the petitioner by the said Upazila Nirbahi Officer under Memo No. 1 Matsya Bala/84/ 90/ 127/ 1(2) dated 19.6.90 in respect of Sarai Beel Jalmahal which were impugned by the respondent No.1 in Writ Petition No. 2551 of 1990 as, Annexures-'I' and 'L' respectively. It is also admitted that the Assistant Judge by his order dated 31.10.90 rejected the plaint of respondent No. 1 in Title Suit No. 12 of 1990 on the ground that there was no cause of action, and the said respondent in its affidavit-in-opposition has not stated that it had no knowledge of the order of the Assistant Judge and therefore had full knowledge of the said order dated 31.10.90 rejecting the plaint when the affidavit of the writ petition was sworn on 22.11.90 and on 26.11.90 when the Rule Nisi was obtained. This deliberate suppression of material fact of the rejection of plaint by the civil Court and the false statement to the effect that the suit was pending and that the suit would be withdrawn by the respondent, is a fraud committed on this Court by the respondent No. 1. It further appears that after suppressing the fact of rejection of the plaint by the Assistant Judge and obtaining a Rule Nisi from this Court, the respondent No. 1 filed a review petition before the said Assistant Judge for review of his order dated 31.10.90 which -was rejected by the Assistant Judge on 28.11.90, and against that order the respondent filed Title Appeal No.1 of 1991 before the District Judge, Sylhet, All these facts were also suppressed after obtaining the Rule Nisi, and thereby the respondent continued to deceive and mislead this Court. The contention of the respondent that the order dated 31.10.90 passed by the Assistant Judge was improper and erroneous and "would be cured before the learned Assistant Judge by filing an application" was not followed up until the Rule Nisi and injunction order was obtained from this Court. The respondent by suppressing facts was obviously seeking remedy simultaneously in two forums for the same cause of action which it cannot do under law. The judgment pronounced by this Court is normally final and should not be readily disturbed or interfered with by way of review. This Court would be most hesitant to review its judgment when such application is made by a defaulting respondent who failed to appear and controvert the facts stated by the petitioners in the writ petition, but where fraud is alleged to have been committed upon this Court the Court has a duty to review as fraud vitiates all proceedings. In the case of Grindlays Bank Limited Vs. Murree Brewery Company Limited reported in 8 PLR (Lahore) III it was held by a judgment delivered by Muhammad Munir CJ, as he then was, that a judgment or an order, however high or independent the tribunal delivering or making it and however exclusive its jurisdiction, is a nullity if it be proved that it was obtained by fraud. It was further held that a lower Court in a suit properly constituted, is certainly competent to set aside a judgment of a higher tribunal if it be proved that such judgment was obtained by fraud; it must a fortiori follow that a Judge of the High Court, sitting singly, has jurisdiction under section 151, Code of Civil Procedure, to vacate an order passed by a Division Bench, of which he was one member, provided the issue whether the order was obtained by fraud, properly comes up before him. In appropriate cases, it is the duty of the Court that has seisin of the case to recall suo motu an order procured by fraud.
